additional_context:
[Council feedback on the previous definition]
Note: this review judged a trace from kinematic_tracer_v2; the current tracer is kinematic_tracer_v3, which adds per-action emphasis and sides and one_sided_limbs. Where a suggestion only works around a limit of the older tracer, use the current fields instead.
From model_reviewer:
- authoring_response.assumptions[2] / proposed_definition.kinematic_profile.primary_joint_actions: The assumption says the wrist rotation is omitted because the schema has no matching action. The table does have radioulnar_joint/pronation and radioulnar_joint/supination. The source instruction explicitly says 'Rotate your wrist as you do so', so a source-stated movement is dropped on an incorrect justification. The frames do not show the forearm rotation direction, so the omission is unresolved rather than settled. That leaves the forearm pattern (pronator and supinator muscles) unsupported. Suggested correction: Decide from the frames and instructions whether the clean needs a radioulnar pronation or supination action, and add it or justify excluding it without claiming the schema lacks the action. Remove the false statement about schema vocabulary.
- proposed_definition.kinematic_profile.stabilization_demands: The right frame shows the bell racked at the shoulder with the elbow flexed and the upper arm held against the load, while the other bell hangs. The profile has no shoulder-level demand or action: no shoulder_position_hold, glenohumeral_stabilization or scapular_stabilization, and no glenohumeral action for the pull and rack path. The tracer therefore returns zero for the deltoids, the latissimus, the rotator cuff and the serratus anterior. A loaded rack hold and a bell pulled close to the body should engage at least some of these, so the tracer's muscle pattern is materially incomplete. Suggested correction: Add shoulder demands that match the frames, for example shoulder_position_hold for the racked bell and scapular_stabilization or glenohumeral_stabilization. Consider a glenohumeral action if the upper arm visibly moves in the pull. Then re-check the tracer profile.
[End of council feedback]

assumptions: The movement is an alternating single-bell clean from a double-kettlebell hang. Each side is cleaned in turn, so both arms work over a set and laterality is bilateral.
The legs and hips drive the clean through hip, knee and ankle extension. The ankle contribution is a minor assist.
The arms pull the bell to the shoulder, so elbow flexion, glenohumeral flexion and scapular elevation are assist actions. The legs and hips move the load.

Radioulnar pronation and supination are omitted by judgment, not because the vocabulary lacks them. The palm faces the body in both frames, the net rotation looks small and its direction is not visible, so no confident pronation or supination can be assigned.
The racked bell needs shoulder_position_hold and scapular_stabilization. Grip and wrist_stability apply because the load is held in the hand.
The spine stays neutral under load, so the trunk works through anti_flexion_spine. Anti_rotation_torso applies because the load alternates between sides.
Because the arms alternate, one_sided_limbs is empty and all actions use working sides, which count on both limbs over the set.
classification_reasons: The frames show a standing double-kettlebell hang clean. Frame 1 is the hinged start with both bells hanging between the feet. Frame 2 is one bell racked at the shoulder while the other hangs.
Hip, knee and ankle extension, the elbow pull, the shrug and the rack hold can all be represented with the available vocabulary.
The instruction to 'rotate your wrist' does not need a radioulnar action here. Both frames show the palm facing the body, so the net forearm rotation looks small and its direction is not visible.
